responsibility: This module implements GCC’s link-time optimization front end and runtime: it reads GIMPLE/IPA intermediate language from object-file LTO sections, merges declarations, types, symbol tables, and callgraph state from many inputs into one whole-program view, and then drives the three LTO execution modes—regular LTO, whole-program analysis (WPA), and local transformation (LTRANS). Its main file groups cover synthetic language/front-end integration for streamed GIMPLE, shared reader and deserialization support, symbol-resolution and prevailing-definition merging, partition construction for WHOPR-style parallel LTRANS, and object-section I/O for embedding and extracting IL in native object files; alongside that, it includes the standalone lto-dump inspection tool plus the driver/build/option glue that connects lto1 and related commands to GCC’s build system and command-line machinery. Overall, gcc/lto is the subsystem that bridges GCC’s middle end with linker-time whole-program compilation, partitioning, and LTO object handling.
